newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Smaller NZ bond market to push funds offshore - ANZ.
newsitem.headline: Smaller NZ bond market to push funds offshore - ANZ.

text.p: An expected contraction in the size of the New Zealand government bond market will cause funds to flow into offshore bonds and to the riskier equities market, ANZ Funds Management said on Wednesday.
General manager Anthony Quirk told the New Zealand Press Association that as government debt reduced and the bond market contracted new corporate debt issue was unlikely to compensate.
"There is a limit to how many good corporates there are that institutions want to invest in," Quirk said.
Local government did provide another avenue as debt levels increased there.
"What you will see is institutions will look to New Zealand for increasing equity investments," Quirk said.
"The wild card is if there is a change of regime or a change in government policy and they start to run deficits again."
Such movements mitigated against New Zealand First's proposed compulsory superannuation scheme, which was intended to increase local investment in New Zealand.
New Zealand First is the junior partner in the Coalition Government with the National Party.
Australia's compulsory scheme meant there was more venture capital there and such a scheme here would see the funds generated looking for a home other than the bond market.

"(Fund managers) will firstly look to New Zealand, to see what they can find here -- corporate debt, venture capital and new shares listed on the stock exchange -- and if that's not an available avenue you'll see an increasing amount go offshore," Quirk said.
A move from bonds to equities was not "like-for-like" in terms of risk.
"If you wanted bond-for-bond you would have to go overseas, so it would be working against what NZ First are looking at."

Visiting director of Barclays Global Investors' fixed income investment, Michel Gonnard, said the debt market was too small to even be included in the key Salomon World Bond Index, which meant index fund managers would overlook New Zealand.
Barclays manages ANZ's world bond portfolio.
Gonnard noted governments running deficits that put their debt markets on the index got international capital whereas New Zealand missed out.
However, he said borrowing was becoming more global and this would support eurobond issues here.
Quirk said ANZ used Barclays to reduce risk rather than chase high yields.
